evidence: src/domain/errors.ts declares DomainValidationError and TaskAlreadyDoneError. These are the only error types, and project.ts, user.ts, task.ts and task-status.ts all use them.

src/domain/task-status.ts defines TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and parseTaskStatus as the single source of truth for status values. task.ts (NewTask.status, Task.currentStatus) and task-repository.ts (TaskFilter.status) both import TaskStatus.
src/domain/project.ts, src/domain/user.ts and src/domain/task.ts all use a private constructor with a static create() factory that validates input, so entity construction is consistent.

src/domain/project-repository.ts, src/domain/user-repository.ts and src/domain/task-repository.ts expose the same nextId/save/findById port shape. TaskRepository also adds findByProject with TaskFilter.
src/domain/task.ts Task.markDone is the only place that enforces the already-done invariant, and it throws TaskAlreadyDoneError.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain files all serve one concern: the core domain model of the task-management system. That covers the entities (Project, User, Task), the TaskStatus value type, the repository ports for each aggregate, and the domain errors. The abstractions are used consistently. Every entity has a private constructor and a static create factory that validates input and throws DomainValidationError. Each repository interface follows the same nextId/save/findById shape. The status values are defined once, in TASK_STATUSES / TaskStatus / parseTaskStatus, and both task.ts and task-repository.ts reuse them instead of redefining them. The rule that a task cannot be completed twice lives only in Task.markDone, which throws TaskAlreadyDoneError. Project.create and User.create both trim the name and reject an empty one, but this is a small per-entity check with its own error message, not a shared invariant that is being duplicated. Nothing in the module bypasses its own abstractions.
